title: Haitian migrants changed this town - Trump's deportation drive is reshaping it again
summary:
In this closely fought midterm election campaign, the small town of Springfield, Ohio, has become a symbol of modern America.
To President Donald Trump, Springfield crystallises America's problems due to years of unchecked immigration.
Today, he says his mass deportation drive means its people are "getting their town back".
But to others, Springfield represents a well-known cycle in the story of modern America.
But in June, the Supreme Court upheld the Trump administration's decision to end TPS for some 350,000 Haitians in the US.

title: Lawyer caught by BBC offering to make illegal-worker fine go away
summary:
A solicitor has been secretly filmed by the BBC explaining how he could make a £45,000 illegal-working fine go away.
Mohammad Alias Yousaf - also known as Alias - made the claim to an undercover reporter, who was posing as a mini-mart owner facing a fine for employing an illegal worker.
At least £150m is currently owed to the government in uncollected illegal-working fines, according to Home Office figures obtained by the BBC.
Many business owners do not take the fines seriously, a law enforcement official has told us anonymously.
She told us she had seen immigration fine notices, "some worth £40,000, stuffed in a box" on a mini-mart counter.

title: US jails Guatemalan man for 30 years over deadly smuggling operation

He was first arrested in Guatemala in August 2024, as part of a cross-border effort to dismantle the human-smuggling network.
By the time the truck was driving from Laredo, Texas, to San Antonio – a distance of 250km (155 miles) – prosecutors say the air conditioning had stopped functioning.
Felipe Orduna-Torres, identified as the leader of the operation in the US, was sentenced to life in prison in a federal court in San Antonio in June 2025.
The I-35 highway near where the truck was found runs through San Antonio from the Mexican border.

title: Trump administration says it has revoked over 300,000 visas
summary:
By Kanishka SinghWASHINGTON, Oct 20 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump's administration has revoked over 300,000 US visas during his second term, the ‌State Department said on Tuesday as the federal government continues its ‌sweeping immigration crackdown.
The number showed an acceleration in the pace of visa revocations in recent ​weeks.
In announcing the latest number on X, State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said the Trump administration "has revoked more ​visas at ​a faster pace than any administration ​in history."

While Trump campaigned in 2024 on ​stopping illegal immigration, his ‌administration has also made legal immigration more difficult — for example ​by imposing expensive fees for certain work visas.

title: Mahmoud Khalil takes deportation fight to the US Supreme Court
summary:
Share Mahmoud Khalil takes deportation fight to the US Supreme Court on social mediaPro-Palestine activist Mahmoud Khalil has petitioned the United States Supreme Court to review a court ruling that could pave the way for his re-arrest and deportation.
That court had ruled that federal law should have prohibited lower courts from ordering Khalil’s release from immigration detention in June 2025.
A permanent US resident and former Columbia University graduate student, Khalil was arrested inside the student housing complex where he lived with his wife, a US citizen.
He has fought his deportation both in the immigration court system and in the federal district court system, where he has filed a habeas corpus case.
In April, the Board of Immigration Appeals denied his appeal in the immigration court system and issued a final order of removal in his case.
